title: Bitcoin Drops Below $86K as Investors Shift to BCH and ZEC – Live Updates】
body:
Bitcoin’s price slipped back below the $86,000 mark on Monday after briefly touching a fresh intraday high near $87,300, as traders shifted capital toward alternative digital assets. The most notable mover was Bitcoin Cash (BCH), which surged 28% to hover around $349 in a 24‑hour span, while privacy‑focused Zcash (ZEC) climbed roughly 9%. The rally in BCH was sparked by the CME Group’s announcement that it will launch futures contracts for both Bitcoin Cash and the decentralized exchange token Uniswap (UNI) starting October 19, marking the first time the exchange will offer derivatives on a non‑Bitcoin cryptocurrency.

The price correction in Bitcoin came after the cryptocurrency rallied to its highest level of the week, buoyed by a broader risk‑on sentiment across global markets. However, the momentum proved short‑lived as profit‑taking and a reallocation of funds into newly listed futures contracts took hold. Analysts note that the CME listing is likely to attract institutional investors who have been hesitant to engage with assets outside of Bitcoin due to limited regulated exposure. By providing a familiar futures framework, the exchange could lower barriers for large‑scale capital inflows into BCH and, to a lesser extent, other altcoins.

BCH’s 28% jump represents the most dramatic price movement among the major tokens over the past day. The token, which split from Bitcoin in 2017, has long positioned itself as a “peer‑to‑peer electronic cash” alternative, but it has struggled to gain mainstream traction. The CME futures launch is expected to bring heightened liquidity and price discovery to the market, potentially narrowing the spread between spot and derivative prices. Market participants anticipate that the futures will also enable hedging strategies, allowing miners and traders to lock in profits or mitigate downside risk more efficiently.

Zcash’s 9% rise, while modest compared to BCH, underscores a renewed interest in privacy‑centric cryptocurrencies amid growing concerns over regulatory scrutiny and data privacy. ZEC’s unique shielded transaction technology offers anonymity that many investors find appealing in an environment where governments are increasingly scrutinizing crypto transactions. The price uptick may also reflect speculative positioning ahead of potential listings on other regulated platforms, which could further legitimize privacy coins that have historically faced exchange delistings.

The broader crypto market remains sensitive to macroeconomic cues, including U.S. inflation data and central bank policy signals. While Bitcoin’s dip below $86,000 may appear as a minor correction, it highlights the asset’s volatility and the rapid reallocation of capital that can occur when new financial products are introduced. Traders are closely watching the upcoming CME futures launch, as the additional derivative instruments could reshape trading volumes and price dynamics not only for BCH but also for the wider altcoin ecosystem.

Looking ahead, the impact of CME’s futures listings will likely unfold over the coming weeks. If institutional participation spikes, BCH could experience sustained upward pressure, potentially testing the $400 threshold. Conversely, any regulatory setbacks or delays could dampen enthusiasm and prompt a reversal. For Bitcoin, maintaining stability above the $85,000 level will be crucial to preserving confidence among both retail and institutional investors. As the crypto market continues to evolve with new financial infrastructure, the interplay between spot prices and derivative products will remain a key driver of price movements across the sector.
